newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. resolution calls on Israel to pay Qana damages.
newsitem.headline: U.N. resolution calls on Israel to pay Qana damages.

text.p: A resolution adopted by a U.N. committee requires Israel to pay more than $1.7 million for damage resulting from its shelling of a U.N. base at Qana, in southern Lebanon, last year in which about 100 civilians taking refuge were killed.

The draft, dealing with the financing of the U.N. Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL), was approved on Saturday by a vote of 107 to 2, with three abstentions by the Assembly's administrative and budgetary committee. Voting against were Israel and the United States. Abstaining were Japan, Russia and Ukraine.
A separate vote was taken on the paragraph in the resolution dealing specifically with damages for the Qana incident, which was approved by 58 to 2 (Israel and the United States) with 52 abstentions.

Under the resolution, Israel would have to pay $844,318 for damage to U.N. property directly attributable to the April 18, 1996 shelling. It would also have to pay $880,300 for the relocation of the Fijian battalion of UNIFIL, which had been based at Qana.

The resolution, which was submitted by Tanzania on behalf of the the so-called "Group of 77" developing countries -- now totalling 132 members -- and China, now goes to the Assembly plenary for endorsement, probably next Friday.

The budget for UNIFIL for the 12-month period from July 1, 1997 to June 30, 1998, is more than $126 million. The force, established in 1978, comprises some 4,500 troops and 490 civilians. It has an accumulated deficit of about $177 million because of unpaid assessments by U.N. members.

A U.N. inquiry last year found that Israel's shelling of the Qana camp, during a drive against Hizbollah guerrillas who had fired rockets into northern Israel, was unlikely to have been the result of gross technical or procedural errors, though that could not be completely ruled out.

Israel said the camp, in which about 100 sheltering Lebanese civilians were killed and many others were wounded, was hit accidentally when artillery on the Israel-Lebanon border shelled positions near the U.N. camp from which mortar fire had been directed at an Israeli patrol.
